conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve been feeling really nauseous, especially when I eat or drink. I threw up once last night. And I have this sharp pain in my upper belly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. How long has this been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s been getting worse over the last two days. I’ve been trying lorazepam like I usually do, but it’s not helping this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any fever, blood in your vomit, or diarrhea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No blood, no diarrhea. I’ve had chills, but my temperature hasn’t gone above 97.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I also see from your clinic visit earlier that there was a mix-up with your medications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I was taking three fluconazole pills and only one prednisone. I thought the pills looked different. I didn’t realize I had it backwards.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. You’re supposed to take more prednisone and just one fluconazole. That mistake may have made your graft-versus-host disease harder to control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh no. Is that why I’m feeling so sick?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It could be part of it. We’ve restarted your prednisone at the right dose—60 mg daily. But the high dose of steroids can also irritate your stomach, which might explain the nausea and pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s the medicine helping me but also making me feel worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’re going to treat the stomach irritation while keeping your immune system under control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll increase your pantoprazole to twice a day and start a new medication called sucralfate. It coats the stomach to help heal the irritation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds good. Will I need any tests?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll do a CT scan of your abdomen to make sure there’s nothing else going on, like an infection or blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I’m glad we’re checking everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. Your CT scan came back. Good news—it shows no signs of infection, blockage, or other problems in your abdomen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. So it’s really just the stomach irritation?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. The scan was completely normal. Your symptoms are most likely due to gastritis from the increased steroid dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the chills? Are those related too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They could be. Sometimes nausea and discomfort can make you feel chilled, even without a fever. We’re not seeing signs of infection in your labs either.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I just reviewed your labs from this morning. Your liver enzymes are a bit high, but they’re at your usual baseline. We think that’s related to your GVHD, not a new problem.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So nothing new to worry about?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at all. Your tacrolimus level is good, and your blood counts are stable. You’re responding well to the treatment for your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I do feel a little better. The nausea isn’t as bad this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. We’ll keep you on the sucralfate and higher-dose pantoprazole to let your stomach heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my prednisone? Will I stay on 60 mg?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep it at 60 mg for now to control your GVHD, but we’ll watch for side effects. We’ll also make sure you and your husband understand all your medications before you go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please. I don’t want to make that mistake again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go over them together. We also adjusted your oxycodone—now it’s 20 mg twice a day for your hip pain, which should be enough.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. My hip pain is chronic, and that dose usually works.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. I just got the final report from your CT scan. It confirms no acute issues in your abdomen. The spleen and lymph nodes show old changes, likely from past infections, but nothing active.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Like TB? Because I had the BCG vaccine years ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. The calcifications are consistent with that. No treatment needed—it’s just a reminder of your history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you today. Your symptoms have improved, and everything looks stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What changes should I expect with my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll start sucralfate four times a day, take pantoprazole twice daily, and stay on prednisone at 60 mg for now. We’ll taper it later. Oxycodone is now 20 mg twice a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your oncologist soon. They’ll help manage your prednisone taper and GVHD. Call if nausea returns or you have new symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel much better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’re glad we could help. Take care, and follow those instructions closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—your liver tests are still a bit high, but we believe it’s due to GVHD, not a new issue. We’ll keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I understand. I’ll keep up with my appointments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. You’re doing well. We’ll get your discharge papers ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll have a nurse go over your medications one more time with you and your husband before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please. I want to make sure I get it right this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. Safety first. We’re here to help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll see you in follow-up, but call sooner if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, and get some rest at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.
